findings.title: Retirement needs separate runtime, work and historical-code frontiers
findings.goodPattern: Expose no-new-work, no-running-pins, cleanup-complete and historical/replay/query retention as separate observations with an owner and age.
findings.badPattern: Delete a deployment or report full retirement solely because an open-operation count reaches zero.
findings.counterexample: Temporal Drained can coexist with closed-workflow query demand inside retention; delayed reclamation callbacks can remain pending.
findings.qualification: Close last ordinary operation, then query retained history and test actual supported behavior after executor stop; delay cleanup separately.

findings.title: Code pinning does not pin shared state or every remote dependency
findings.goodPattern: State owner declares mixed-version readers/writers; dependency contract records independent remote versioning boundaries.
findings.badPattern: Treat invocation deployment pin as a global snapshot of every service and persistent record.
findings.counterexample: Restate Virtual Object state survives versions; Temporal Independent Activities use their own Task Queue version.
findings.qualification: Hold v1 while v2 writes shared schema; issue an independent downstream call after downstream rollout; require explicitly chosen compatibility or rejection.

findings.title: A recovery strategy must keep its durable identity across restart
findings.goodPattern: Own one update attempt identity and persist the exact snapshot/replay selection before executing it; distinguish pending retry from terminal failure.
findings.badPattern: After restart reselect whatever latest snapshot or revision is now available and call it the original attempt.
findings.counterexample: Golem v1.6 documentation selects baseline when queued update runs and durably retains that selection; automatic and manual modes have different stopping boundaries.
findings.qualification: Released selection code and named upstream integration tests corroborate the mechanism. Those tests were not executed; no Golem service was started.

findings.title: Bound retention and backlog without inventing completion
findings.goodPattern: Account retained generations, operations and cleanup separately; use admission/backpressure or explicit supported cancel/restart policy.
findings.badPattern: Keep unlimited old versions for perfect draining, or reclaim after a timer while readers still own resources.
findings.counterexample: A stalled RCU reader blocks grace periods; update callbacks can accumulate faster than reclamation. Restate recommends bounded handler durations because old endpoints must remain available.
findings.qualification: Hold a real reader/stream while repeatedly preparing versions; prove candidate admission is bounded and old resource remains valid.

findings.title: A CLI drain preflight is not a server-side safe-deletion transaction
findings.goodPattern: Expose whether a backend enforces graceful deletion; finish stop-admission and retention checks through its existing authority.
findings.badPattern: Display a preflight as an atomic retirement guarantee or invoke force behind a generic safe-delete abstraction.
findings.counterexample: Restate 1.8.1 CLI checks deployment status then sends force=true; server rejects force=false, and bulk_delete_validation asserts that rejection.
findings.qualification: Upstream tests inspected, not executed. A concurrent schema/routing change between query and delete is a proposed negative probe, not a reproduced incident.

findings.title: Delete propagation and reactivation can race even when the public state machine looks simple
findings.goodPattern: Use the existing authority's ordered transition/revision controls; retain tombstones or serialize unversioned forget propagation with republish.
findings.badPattern: Treat deleting the local routing entry as globally completed cleanup, then immediately revive the same identity.
findings.counterexample: Temporal serializes outstanding propagation before forgetting; relevant history-version/reactivation branches wait for delete propagation because the deleted flag lacks revision protection. Other version data has revision protection.
findings.qualification: Inspect TestDeleteVersion_ThenRecreateByPolling and race branches; no Temporal server started.

findings.title: Native context tracking is usable; resource lifetime and revocation remain separate
findings.goodPattern: Capture a frozen operation identity at admission and bind delayed continuation or iterator consumption where context would otherwise be chosen again.
findings.badPattern: Assume snapshot clones the store, bind all future user actions to the registration version, or treat context as an ownership lease.
findings.counterexample: 5/5 native cases: mutable snapshot reflects mutation; unbound iterator uses consumer context; bound old context survives native file close while read fails EBADF.
findings.qualification: Node 24.22.3 only; process/worker/browser propagation and cancellation not exercised. Runtime ownership must remain with the host's existing lifetime mechanism.

findings.title: A cleanup callback can require old code after all its readers have finished
findings.goodPattern: Expose distinct receipts for operations quiescent and callback/resource cleanup completed; stop re-enqueuing producers before the final cleanup barrier.
findings.badPattern: Free the runtime on readers-zero or claim a timeout proves cleanup; wait for finalization while a callback can enqueue more work.
findings.counterexample: Linux module unload needs rcu_barrier after blocking new callbacks; synchronize_rcu alone does not wait for callbacks. Crossbeam defer_destroy gives no deadline.
findings.qualification: Analogy for lifecycle obligations, not a TS RCU implementation or proof of JS memory-order requirements.

findings.title: Compatibility policy and version preference are separate decisions
findings.goodPattern: Select among versions whose declared contract/schema compatibility is accepted; separately decide minimum/latest/cohort preference and per-session pin.
findings.badPattern: Treat numeric version order or semver range as evidence that saved state and all operations can be replayed.
findings.counterexample: Orleans default backward director tests requestedVersion <= currentVersion; MinimumVersion then chooses minimum accepted available number. Metadata cannot infer application semantics.
findings.qualification: Upstream UpgradeTests inspected only. Require mixed old/new reader-writer qualification for the actual plugin state.

feedback.status: completed lane; native qualification and limits recorded

findings.title: Force registration does not attest application retirement
findings.status: pinned source inspected; historical issue not reproduced
findings.action: Reuse runtime loader and hooks; preserve immutable entry/chunk/dependency identity and separate owner cleanup.
findings.applicability: Remote modules with shared-runtime closure under a real federation bundler.
findings.falsifier: Load both releases; invoke a retained old export; trace chunk identities and shared provider selection; inspect actual owner resources.

findings.title: Timeout rejection does not stop the underlying lifecycle
findings.action: Expose stalled cleanup and eventual completion separately; keep actual cleanup owner.
findings.applicability: Application/parcel lifecycle composition, not arbitrary capability functions.
findings.falsifier: Delay unmount past deadline, then release it; inspect late effects after wrapper rejection.

findings.title: Undo capture can span a version boundary
findings.status: confirmed released Yjs public API; strict TypeScript 7.0.2
findings.action: Keep stable document/history owner and deliberately stop capture at meaningful semantic boundaries.
findings.applicability: Compatible collaborative document schema and retained UndoManager.
findings.falsifier: Adjacent edits from different tracked origins yield one undo entry unless stopCapturing is called.

findings.title: History-origin filtering and destroy are not write authorization
findings.status: confirmed released API, including deliberate post-destroy misuse negative control
findings.action: Validate authority before mutation at the state owner; avoid giving retired plugins raw mutable document references.
findings.applicability: A plugin/state adapter with control over the real mutation ingress; no in-process sandbox claim.
findings.falsifier: Removed origin or destroyed retained text can still change document and the changes transfer to a peer.

findings.title: Exact view disposal can preserve draft and undo history
findings.action: View owns exact subscriptions; document/history owner outlives compatible views.
findings.applicability: Compatible shared document; not proof of DOM or renderer behavior.
findings.falsifier: Retired observer receives a later edit, or undo state is lost when only the binding changes.

findings.title: Document restoration does not restore local UndoManager history
findings.status: confirmed real public binary encoding and merge
findings.action: Expose content restore, history reset/retention, and draft discard as distinct policies.
findings.applicability: Current Yjs document codec; not a claim that another history persistence layer is impossible.
findings.falsifier: Restore content to a fresh document/history and inspect undo availability before accepting session continuity.

findings.title: Relative cursor state handles compatible sequence edits
findings.status: confirmed public relative-position codec and real peer update
findings.action: Use existing editor/CRDT binding when needed; handle null resolution explicitly.
findings.applicability: Sequence-relative positions in supported document types; no IME/focus/render qualification.
findings.falsifier: Remote prepend shifts numeric index while encoded relative position preserves logical end; deletion of referenced type needs fallback.

findings.title: Fallback load success is not requested candidate readiness
findings.status: pinned load path plus official hooks inspected
findings.action: Expose original error and recovered fallback; candidate, selected provider, and useful output remain distinct.
findings.applicability: Loader hooks expose these facts; semantic readiness remains product-defined.
findings.falsifier: A failed real remote resolves to fallback while diagnostics incorrectly claim candidate ready.

findings.title: Active code removal needs explicit eligibility and a supported fallback boundary
findings.status: pinned VS Code path and official runtime profiles
findings.action: Advertise capability/host eligibility and actual restart consequences; keep browser and Node execution profiles explicit.
findings.applicability: IDE host architecture as reference, not embedding VS Code as a generic library.
findings.falsifier: Restart the chosen host with dirty documents and work; compare the actual surviving state to the preview.

findings.title: Compile-time DI modules and runtime-installed extensions are different units
findings.status: official Theia documentation, including deprecated page warning
findings.action: Separate composition modules from API-bound runtime plugins; do not use legacy direct-UI plugin examples as compatibility commitments.
findings.applicability: Architecture analogy; Theia implementation was not executed.
findings.falsifier: Attempt dynamic replacement through the chosen supported extension API and verify the claimed boundary.

findings.title: Custom-element registries do not provide arbitrary redefinition
findings.status: normative specification inspected; browser matrix not executed
findings.action: Use supported fresh subtree/registry or generation tag when Web Components fit; qualify move/disconnect behavior.
findings.applicability: Product browser matrix and chosen component mechanism.
findings.falsifier: Repeat define, preserve/move existing element, and inspect reactions in every supported browser.

findings.title: Diagnostic status must remain a bounded read-only projection
findings.status: design inference informed by loader provenance and state-owner probe
findings.action: Use owner revisions, snapshots, coalesced component status, and bounded diagnostics; commands return to authority.
findings.applicability: Existing telemetry/event/state owners, no second manager or state store.
findings.falsifier: After out-of-order events or reconnect, projection should resync and cannot authorize an obsolete transition.

findings.title: Rollback selects code; Undo changes content
findings.status: design inference; no migration or rollback protocol executed
findings.action: Retain old artifact eligibility separately from current document/history/schema compatibility.
findings.applicability: Versioned implementation updates with live user drafts.
findings.falsifier: Old code must reject incompatible current state or use an explicit migration; undo must not accidentally select implementation.

findings.title: Old artifacts, documents, history, views, and executors need distinct retention
findings.status: design requirement; no prolonged-edit memory measurement
findings.action: Use existing owners to define budgets and pin reasons; release views without clearing user content or unlimited history retention.
findings.falsifier: Prolonged editing and repeated replacement should expose retained owner counts and explicit pin reasons; no leak-free claim follows from seven cases.

boundaries.finding: Separate-library direction matches current organization library-first policy; old integration-only estimates are not estimates of the library.
boundaries.consequence: Record a successor owner decision, retaining single-owner lifecycle/authority boundaries.

boundaries.finding: New production repositories require full FMS v1.1 and real Foundation/native gates at the first reviewed bootstrap; SDK/library is not an exemption.
boundaries.consequence: A research checkpoint can precede production bootstrap but cannot claim production admission based on documentation links.

boundaries.finding: Feature ownership is mandatory; feature=package and empty architecture scaffolding are not.
boundaries.consequence: Start a small number of cohesive modules with real features, split Effect/runtime adapters only at real dependency or lifetime boundaries.

boundaries.finding: Get Modular native Effect construction is optional and distinct from ordinary Promise construction; app-native Effect adoption is separate.
boundaries.consequence: Keep neutral data/authority contracts and ordinary TypeScript external consumers; add an optional native Effect execution surface without inventing a universal Task/Fiber/Scope abstraction.

boundaries.finding: Resources cooperative cleanup debt/retry and native Effect Scope/finalizer semantics are different contracts.
boundaries.consequence: Runtime capability profiles must not strengthen backend guarantees; separate revocation, operation settlement, stop observation, physical cleanup and unresolved effects.

boundaries.finding: Private lifecycle kernel owns single-agent synchronous generation/lease bookkeeping only and is not a released general runtime.
boundaries.consequence: Do not copy/deep-import; official public-owner route or explicit blocked capability before production use.

boundaries.finding: Layer memoization uses Layer identity in MemoMap. Fresh Scope and fresh GM mapper identities do not clone borrowed values or private captured Layers.
boundaries.consequence: Generation-specific configuration/state and deliberately shared application resources require explicit identity/ownership.

boundaries.finding: RcMap owner close closes currently indexed entries irrespective of refCount; invalidate removes the old entry and defers closing while references remain.
boundaries.consequence: A cache/refcount mechanism is not the whole generation-retention authority; avoid duplicate authoritative counts.

boundaries.finding: ManagedRuntime disposal completion Deferred is completed with Exit.void in ensuring, so later dispose does not replay first close failure.
boundaries.consequence: A stable portable terminal receipt must preserve the first observed outcome; do not imply retryable Effect Scope cleanup.

boundaries.finding: XState5.33.4 pure transition API collects actions without running them; Promise actors abort and ignore later resolve/reject when stopped.
boundaries.consequence: Pure statechart engine is a conditional reuse candidate; live actor stop cannot own late foreign acquisition cleanup by itself.

boundaries.finding: Start one portable module with planning/replacement/observation features; split real runtime and optional native dependency lifecycles, not every feature into a package.
boundaries.consequence: Preserve one update policy and existing authority/resource owners; grow from an external-consumer vertical slice.

boundaries.finding: Ordinary and native Effect profiles may share finite domain-specific update facts/decisions; avoid both Promise-erasing native semantics and a universal task DSL.
boundaries.consequence: Select two execution drivers only if two real consumers demonstrate the requirement; qualify cross-driver conformance.

boundaries.finding: Registry metadata confirms @get-modular/effect0.1.1 with exactEffect4.1.4 and Core/Assembly^0.8.0 peers.
boundaries.consequence: Do not conflate existence metadata with installed artifact or production behavior qualification.

boundaries.finding: Current stable XState tag inspected is5.33.4;v6 persistence documentation is beta and has different APIs.
boundaries.consequence: Do not mix release profiles or infer transactional external-effect recovery from persisted actor snapshots.

boundaries.finding: First portable one-mode/one-runtime library band:P900–1800/I500–1000/T1800–3500/docs-tooling600–1200, estimateconfidence4/10; incremental adapter/native/durable bands separate.
boundaries.consequence: OldP0/I150–350 estimate is integration-only; all bands are planning judgments, not measuredLOC/reliability.
